title: MATH GAOKAO - 136
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an angle from degrees to radians.
questions.question: Convert \(120^\circ\) to radians.
questions.explanation:
Use the conversion factor
\[
180^\circ=\pi.
\]
Thus
\[
120^\circ=120\cdot \frac{\pi}{180}
=\frac{120\pi}{180}
=\frac{2\pi}{3}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
120^\circ=\frac{2\pi}{3}.
\]
questions.hint: Multiply the degree measure by \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) and simplify.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an angle from radians to degrees.
questions.question: Convert \(\frac{5\pi}{6}\text{ radians}\) to degrees.
questions.explanation:
Use the conversion factor
\[
\pi=180^\circ.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{5\pi}{6}
=\frac{5\pi}{6}\cdot \frac{180^\circ}{\pi}
=\frac{5\cdot 180^\circ}{6}
=150^\circ.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\frac{5\pi}{6}=150^\circ.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Compute arc length using a central angle in radians.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(10\text{ cm}\). Find the length of the arc subtended by a central angle of \(\frac{\pi}{5}\text{ radians}\).
questions.explanation:
The arc length formula in radian measure is
\[
s=r\theta.
\]
Substitute \(r=10\) and \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{5}\):
\[
s=10\cdot \frac{\pi}{5}=2\pi.
\]
Therefore, the arc length is
\[
2\pi \text{ cm}.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Compute the area of a sector using a central angle in radians.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(6\text{ cm}\). Find the area of the sector with central angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}\).
questions.explanation:
The sector area formula in radian measure is
\[
A=\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta.
\]
Substitute \(r=6\) and \(\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}\):
\[
A=\frac{1}{2}(6)^2\cdot \frac{\pi}{3}
=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 36\cdot \frac{\pi}{3}
=6\pi.
\]
Therefore, the area is
\[
6\pi \text{ cm}^2.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Determine the reference angle for an angle given in radians.
questions.question: Find the reference angle of \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\).
questions.explanation:
The angle \(\frac{7\pi}{6}\) lies in the third quadrant because
\[
\pi<\frac{7\pi}{6}<\frac{3\pi}{2}.
\]
For an angle in the third quadrant, the reference angle is found by subtracting \(\pi\):
\[
\frac{7\pi}{6}-\pi
=\frac{7\pi}{6}-\frac{6\pi}{6}
=\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]
Therefore, the reference angle is
\[
\frac{\pi}{6}.
\]
questions.hint: Identify the quadrant first, then subtract \(\pi\) or \(2\pi\) as appropriate.

questions.learningObjective: Find a coterminal angle between \(0\) and \(2\pi\).
questions.question: Find the angle between \(0\) and \(2\pi\) that is coterminal with \(\frac{13\pi}{4}\).
questions.explanation:
Coterminal angles differ by multiples of \(2\pi\). Subtract \(2\pi\):
\[
\frac{13\pi}{4}-2\pi
=\frac{13\pi}{4}-\frac{8\pi}{4}
=\frac{5\pi}{4}.
\]
Since
\[
0<\frac{5\pi}{4}<2\pi,
\]
the required coterminal angle is
\[
\frac{5\pi}{4}.
\]
questions.hint: Subtract \(2\pi\) until the angle lies between \(0\) and \(2\pi\).

questions.learningObjective: Convert an angle from degrees to radians.
questions.question: Convert \(210^\circ\) to radians.
questions.explanation:
Use the conversion factor
\[
180^\circ=\pi.
\]
Thus
\[
210^\circ=210\cdot \frac{\pi}{180}
=\frac{210\pi}{180}
=\frac{7\pi}{6}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
210^\circ=\frac{7\pi}{6}.
\]
questions.hint: Multiply by \(\frac{\pi}{180}\) and simplify the fraction.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate a trigonometric function at a standard radian angle.
questions.question:
Evaluate
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{3}.
\]
questions.explanation:
The angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\) is \(60^\circ\). From the standard values of trigonometric functions,
\[
\sin 60^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\sin\frac{\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Find the central angle given arc length and radius.
questions.question: A circle has radius \(4\text{ cm}\) and an arc of length \(2\pi\text{ cm}\). Find the central angle in radians.
questions.explanation:
The arc length formula is
\[
s=r\theta.
\]
Substitute \(s=2\pi\) and \(r=4\):
\[
2\pi=4\theta.
\]
Then
\[
\theta=\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]
Therefore, the central angle is
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

questions.learningObjective: Compute angular speed in radians per unit time.
questions.question: A wheel rotates \(30\pi\text{ radians}\) in \(5\text{ minutes}\). Find its angular speed in radians per minute.
questions.explanation:
Angular speed is
\[
\omega=\frac{\text{angle rotated}}{\text{time}}.
\]
Substitute \(30\pi\text{ radians}\) and \(5\text{ minutes}\):
\[
\omega=\frac{30\pi}{5}=6\pi.
\]
Therefore, the angular speed is
\[
6\pi \text{ radians per minute}.
\]
questions.hint: Divide the total angle by the total time.
